free_tier.stated: AMD-only GPU host: the pricing page lists none of H100, A100 80 GB, L40S, RTX 4090 or L4. MI300X virtual machines (1, 2 and 4 GPUs) are USD 2.99 per GPU-hour and 8x MI300X bare metal is USD 3.39 per GPU-hour, billed by the minute; the page names no pricing tier and states no minimum bill. Credits are added to a team before compute is provisioned. A third-party tracker reports a minimum rental of one GPU for one minute and prepaid credits bought by card through Stripe or in USDT and USDC (checked 2026-10-17).

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The one-minute minimum and per-minute billing make this the only 192 GB card sold in units a benchmark can afford, which is what a trial run needs before a multi-hour commitment.
limits_note: Nothing published binds above a single GPU for a single minute; the whole cost is prepaid and the smallest unit is one minute.
binding_note: Nothing published binds above a single GPU for a single minute; the whole cost is prepaid and the smallest unit is one minute.

identity_cost.detail: The vendor's quick-start page signs a user in with an email address and a verification code sent to it, then credits are added to a team before compute is provisioned. Prepaid credits rather than a subscription, and a third-party tracker records payment by card or by USDT and USDC, so a stablecoin balance is an alternative to a card.
